faq.title: Questions we hear a lot
faq.description: Short answers about files, limits, and how the product actually works.

files.a: Files are uploaded for processing and scoped to your anonymous session or account. Downloads use short-lived signed URLs. Temporary files expire after about two hours.

anonymous.a: No. Free covers the same daily limits with or without signing in. An account is optional for history, billing, and API keys.

formats.a: The catalog includes PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, JPG, PNG, and OCR tools. Each tool dropzone shows the formats that tool accepts.

limits.a: Free is 5 operations per day, 25 MB per file, one file at a time, and 50 pages per file — with or without an account. OCR is Pro-only. Pro is $5 per month for unlimited operations and a 1 GB file limit. Files expire after about two hours. Developer API credits are billed separately.

account.a: You get recent activity, billing, and API keys. Daily Free limits stay the same. Tool pages stay the same: upload a file, then download the result.

credits.a: Web operations on Free are capped daily. Pro is $5 per month for unlimited web use. API credits are billed separately on Developer packs and meter programmatic usage.

api.a: Yes. The public v1 API uses the same upload, process, and download flow with an API key. API credit packs are separate from web plans.

privacy.a: Yes. Files are scoped to your session or account, not a shared library. Downloads use short-lived signed URLs rather than public links.

pro.a: Pro is $5 per month. It unlocks OCR, editing, e-sign, and AI tools, removes the daily operation cap, and raises the file size limit to 1 GB.

payment.q: How do payment and cancellation work?
payment.a: Checkout runs through Polar after you sign in. Payment methods, invoices, and cancellation are handled in the Polar customer portal. Yearly API packs are 20% off when that product is configured.

story.title: Who we are
story.lead: We build PDF tools for people who already have a job to finish. This is not a document library, not a place to park files, and not a dashboard you are meant to live in.
story.body: Each tool is its own page: open it, upload a file, download the result. Signed-in accounts get recent activity, billing, and API keys. Anonymous-allowed tools work without an account. Temporary files expire after about two hours — that is the product, not a missing feature.

questions.title: Questions about us
questions.description: Limits, credits, and payment live on the FAQ. These answers are about the product itself.

what.a: PDF tools and a public API. You process a file and download the output. We do not keep a permanent library of your documents.

who.a: SoHappyPDF is an independent product we build and operate. We process files in the cloud, scope them to your session or account, and expire them on a short timer. We do not claim compliance certifications.

why.a: Everyday PDF work should not become storage. A short lifetime keeps the product simple and keeps files from lingering after the job is done.

start.a: Open a tool, drop a file, and download when processing completes. If you need history or the API, create an account.

security.title: Security we actually provide
security.description: These are product controls, not third-party compliance certifications. If a badge is not listed here, we do not claim it.

honest.title: What this page is not
honest.body: SoHappyPDF does not publish third-party audit reports or compliance certifications. This page describes how the product handles files, accounts, and API keys today.

files.title: Files stay scoped and temporary
files.body: Uploads and results are tied to your anonymous session or signed-in account, not a shared library. Downloads use short-lived signed URLs rather than public object links. Temporary files expire after about two hours. Presigned upload and download URLs expire after 15 minutes.

accounts.title: Accounts are authorized on the server
accounts.body: The account area uses email and password authentication. File, conversion, billing, and API key actions are authorized on the server. Client-side checks are not a permission grant.

api.title: API keys are secrets
api.body: Programmatic access uses a Bearer API key. Do not put keys in URLs, browser JavaScript, or source control. If a key leaks, delete it in the account area and create a replacement.

report.title: Report a security issue
report.body: If you find a vulnerability in SoHappyPDF, email us with enough detail to reproduce it. Do not attach customer files. We will not ask you to send API keys or passwords.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: How SoHappyPDF handles files, accounts, payments, and cookies. We keep this aligned with how the product works.

overview.title: What we collect
overview.body: SoHappyPDF processes PDFs and related files so you can convert, merge, compress, and otherwise transform them. We also store the account data needed to sign in, bill a plan, and issue API keys. We do not sell your files or account data.

files.title: Files you upload
files.body: Source files and results are stored in private object storage so the tool can run. They are scoped to your session or account. Temporary files expire after about two hours and are then deleted. The product is not a document archive — download results you need to keep.

accounts.title: Account data
accounts.body: If you create an account we store your email, name if you provide one, a hashed password, session data, recent activity, and API key metadata. We do not store the raw API key after it is shown once.

payments.title: Payments
payments.body: Checkout, invoices, and cards are handled by Polar. SoHappyPDF stores the subscription and credit-pack status needed to enforce Free, Pro, and API entitlements. Card numbers are not stored in SoHappyPDF.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: We use a small set of first-party cookies to remember language, keep an anonymous tool session, and keep you signed in. We do not run advertising pixels or analytics scripts on the marketing or app pages. Details are on the cookies page.

retention.title: How long data stays
retention.body: Tool files are kept for about two hours. Account, billing, and API key records stay until you close the account or we have to keep them for the payment provider or the law. You can ask us to delete an account by email.

processors.title: Who else sees data
processors.body: Files run through our application, worker, and private object storage. Polar processes payments. Hosting and email delivery providers see the technical data needed to run those services. We do not share files with other customers.

contact.title: Privacy questions
contact.body: Email hello@sohappypdf.com. Do not send files to that address — upload them on a tool page if you need them processed.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.description: The rules for using SoHappyPDF’s public tools, accounts, and API. Keep a local copy of any file you still need after processing.

service.title: The service
service.body: SoHappyPDF provides web PDF tools and a public API. You may use anonymous-allowed tools without an account, subject to Free daily limits. Signing in unlocks history, billing, and API keys. We may change features, limits, and prices; current limits are published on Pricing.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.body: You are responsible for the email and password on your account and for any API keys you create. Keep keys secret. Delete a leaked key. We may suspend an account that abuses the service or these terms.

acceptableUse.title: Acceptable use
acceptableUse.body: Do not upload malware, try to break the product, scrape it in a way that harms other users, or use it for unlawful content. You must have the right to process the files you upload. We may refuse or delete jobs that look abusive.

files.title: Files expire
files.body: Uploads and results are temporary processing assets, not a library. They expire after about two hours. If a download link stops working, process the file again. We are not a backup service.

billing.title: Plans and Polar
billing.body: Free and Pro are web plans. API credit packs are billed separately. Checkout and cancellation run through Polar after you sign in. Polar’s portal is where you update cards, download invoices, and cancel. Unused API credits reset at the end of the pack period.

api.title: API
api.body: The public v1 API uses the same tools as the website. Rate limits and key limits follow your web plan. API credits meter programmatic usage only. Do not put API keys in client-side code.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: We may update these terms. The date at the top of this page is the current version. Continued use after an update means you accept the new terms. If you do not, stop using the service and cancel through Polar.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: For product, billing, or API questions, email hello@sohappypdf.com. Do not attach files to that mailbox.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.description: SoHappyPDF uses a small number of first-party cookies to run the site. We do not set advertising or analytics cookies.

overview.title: What we use cookies for
overview.body: Cookies are small text files stored by your browser. We use them only to remember your language, keep anonymous tool usage scoped to your browser, and keep a signed-in session. There is no cookie banner because we do not run optional tracking cookies.

language.title: Language
language.body: Choosing a language sets an httpOnly cookie named NEXT_LOCALE for up to one year so the site stays in that language. You can change it any time from the language control in the footer.

session.title: Sessions
session.body: Anonymous tool use may set a first-party cookie named spdf_anon so files stay attached to your browser instead of a shared pool. Signing in sets account session cookies so the account area can load. These cookies are httpOnly. Signing out clears the account session.

payments.title: Payments
payments.body: Checkout happens on Polar. Polar may set its own cookies on its domain while you pay or manage a subscription. Those cookies are Polar’s, not SoHappyPDF marketing or analytics cookies.

control.title: How to control cookies
control.body: You can delete cookies in your browser. If you block all cookies, language preference and sign-in will not persist. Necessary cookies above are required for those features to work.

developerDocs.title: Build on the same tools
developerDocs.description: Every browser tool is a conversion type. Create an API key, upload with a presigned PUT, then POST /conversions with that type. Poll until the job completes and download the output file.

quickstart.title: Quickstart
quickstart.step1: Create a key in Account → API. It is shown only once.
quickstart.step2: Send Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY on every request. Never put the key in a URL or browser code.
quickstart.step3: POST /files/upload, PUT the bytes to upload.url, then POST /files/'{id}'/complete.
quickstart.step4: POST /conversions with sourceFileId, targetFormat, and type. Use the tool id as type.
quickstart.step5: Poll GET /conversions/'{id}' every two seconds until completed, then POST /files/'{outputFileId}'/download.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.description: Programmatic access uses API keys. Dashboard cookies are for the web app, not integrations.
auth.ruleHeader: Send the key only in the Authorization header.
auth.ruleSecret: Treat the key as a secret. Do not commit it.
auth.ruleBrowser: Do not ship keys in frontend JavaScript.
auth.ruleRevoke: Delete a leaked key in the dashboard and create a replacement.

files.title: Files
files.description: Uploads are presigned. The API never holds the file bytes. Complete the upload before you create a conversion.
files.expiry: Temporary files expire after about two hours. Presigned upload and download URLs expire after 15 minutes.

conversions.title: Conversions
conversions.description: POST /conversions returns 201 and enqueues a worker job. The type field is the tool id. Options go in options. Extra input files go in additionalFileIds, not inside the file bytes.
conversions.pollHint: Poll while status is {pending}. Stop on {done}. When completed, conversion.outputFileId is set.
conversions.idempotency: Send Idempotency-Key (1–128 characters) on create. A replay with the same owner and key returns the original job and does not consume another credit.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Use the tool id as conversion type. The JSON below is the POST /conversions body. Credits come from the catalog. Planned tools are omitted until they ship.

errors.title: Errors
errors.description: Every error uses this envelope. Missing files and conversions both return NOT_FOUND. An expired owned file returns FILE_EXPIRED instead of 404.
errors.retry: 429 includes Retry-After, RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset. Wait, then retry. Do not tight-loop.

limits.title: Limits and credits
limits.description: API credits are separate from web tool credits. Rate limits follow the web plan. Hitting a quota returns 403 PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED.
limits.free: Free: {ops} conversions/day, 25 MB files, {rpm} API requests/minute.
limits.pro: Pro: unlimited conversions, 1 GB files, {rpm} API requests/minute.
limits.credits: Each conversion consumes the tool’s API credit cost. Accounts include {count} API credits each month; buy Developer packs from billing for more.
limits.webhooks: Webhooks are not available. Clients must poll.

notes.extraFilesTopLevel: Pass extra uploads as additionalFileIds on the conversion, after each file is completed.
notes.explicitType: Send type explicitly. The API will not infer this tool from formats alone.
notes.rangesInclusive: Range start and end are inclusive.
notes.ocrLanguage: language is an OCR language code such as eng or tur.
notes.protectSecret: Do not log passwords. Rotate them if a request is captured.
notes.signVisualOnly: This is a visual stamp, not a cryptographic digital signature.
notes.compareSecondFile: Upload both PDFs, then pass the second id in additionalFileIds.

how.question: How do I use this tool?
how.answer: Upload a supported file. If the tool needs no extra options, processing starts automatically. Then download the result when it is ready. An account is not required unless the tool says it is.

account.question: Do I need an account?
account.anonymous: No. You can run this tool without creating an account. Sign in if you want history, billing, and API keys. Daily Free limits stay the same.
account.required: Yes. Sign in before processing. This tool is not available without an account.

editor.propertiesEmpty: Click text on the page to edit it, or select a mark.

merge-pdf.name: Merge PDF
merge-pdf.description: Combine multiple PDF files into one document. Upload the files, set the order, and download a single PDF. No account needed for basic use.

split-pdf.name: Split PDF
split-pdf.description: Split a PDF into a new file with only the pages you need. Select pages visually, then download the result.

extract-pages.name: Extract PDF pages
extract-pages.description: Take selected pages out of a PDF and save the rest as a new file. Choose pages visually, then download.

organize-pdf.name: Organize PDF
organize-pdf.description: Rearrange, rotate, and manage PDF pages in one place, then download the updated file.

remove-pages.name: Remove PDF pages
remove-pages.description: Delete unwanted pages from a PDF and keep the rest in a new file.

reorder-pages.name: Reorder PDF pages
reorder-pages.description: Change the page order of a PDF, then download the rearranged file.

rotate-pdf.name: Rotate PDF
rotate-pdf.description: Rotate one or more pages in a PDF, then download the corrected file.

crop-pdf.name: Crop PDF
crop-pdf.description: Crop page margins and extra space from a PDF, then download the result.

compress-pdf.name: Compress PDF
compress-pdf.description: Reduce PDF file size while keeping the document readable. Choose a compression level and download a smaller PDF.

repair-pdf.name: Repair PDF
repair-pdf.description: Attempt to fix a damaged or unreadable PDF, then download a repaired copy.

pdf-to-pdfa.name: PDF to PDF/A
pdf-to-pdfa.description: Convert a PDF into an archival PDF/A file for longer-term storage.

pdf-to-word.name: PDF to Word
pdf-to-word.description: Convert a PDF into an editable Word document. Upload a PDF and download a DOC or DOCX file.

pdf-to-word-ocr.name: PDF to Word OCR
pdf-to-word-ocr.description: Convert a scanned PDF to Word with OCR so the text can be edited.

pdf-to-powerpoint.name: PDF to PowerPoint
pdf-to-powerpoint.description: Convert a PDF into a PowerPoint presentation you can edit and present.

pdf-to-excel.name: PDF to Excel
pdf-to-excel.description: Convert tables in a PDF into an Excel spreadsheet you can sort and edit.

pdf-to-excel-ocr.name: PDF to Excel OCR
pdf-to-excel-ocr.description: Convert scanned PDF tables to Excel with OCR.

pdf-to-jpg.name: PDF to JPG
pdf-to-jpg.description: Convert PDF pages into JPG images you can save or share.

pdf-to-png.name: PDF to PNG
pdf-to-png.description: Convert PDF pages into PNG images with a transparent or clean background.

pdf-to-txt.name: PDF to text
pdf-to-txt.description: Extract plain text from a PDF and download it as a text file.

word-to-pdf.name: Word to PDF
word-to-pdf.description: Convert a Word document into a PDF you can share or print.

powerpoint-to-pdf.name: PowerPoint to PDF
powerpoint-to-pdf.description: Convert a PowerPoint presentation into a PDF.

excel-to-pdf.name: Excel to PDF
excel-to-pdf.description: Convert an Excel spreadsheet into a PDF.

image-to-pdf.name: Image to PDF
image-to-pdf.description: Combine JPG, PNG, or other images into a single PDF.

jpg-to-pdf.name: JPG to PDF
jpg-to-pdf.description: Convert a JPG image into a PDF file.

png-to-pdf.name: PNG to PDF
png-to-pdf.description: Convert a PNG image into a PDF file.

office-to-pdf.name: Office to PDF
office-to-pdf.description: Convert Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files into PDF.

edit-pdf.name: Edit PDF
edit-pdf.description: Edit existing PDF text, then add highlights, shapes, or images if you need them.

watermark-pdf.name: Watermark PDF
watermark-pdf.description: Add a text or image watermark across every page of a PDF.

page-numbers-pdf.name: Add PDF page numbers
page-numbers-pdf.description: Add page numbers to a PDF, then download the numbered file.

protect-pdf.name: Protect PDF
protect-pdf.description: Add a password so others need it to open or use the PDF.

unlock-pdf.name: Unlock PDF
unlock-pdf.description: Remove password protection from a PDF you own, then download an unlocked copy.

sign-pdf.name: Sign PDF
sign-pdf.description: Add a visual signature image or text stamp. This is not a cryptographic digital signature.

redact-pdf.name: Redact PDF
redact-pdf.description: Permanently black out sensitive text or areas in a PDF before you share it.

compare-pdf.name: Compare PDF
compare-pdf.description: Compare two PDF versions and see what changed.

pdf-forms.name: Fill PDF forms
pdf-forms.description: Fill existing fields in an interactive PDF form, then download the completed file.

web-to-pdf.name: Web to PDF
web-to-pdf.description: Capture a web page as a PDF you can save or share.

scan-to-pdf.name: Scan to PDF
scan-to-pdf.description: Turn scanned images into a single PDF.

pdf-extract.name: Extract PDF content
pdf-extract.description: Extract structured content from a PDF for reuse in other files.

pdf-to-markdown.name: PDF to Markdown
pdf-to-markdown.description: Convert PDF content into Markdown you can edit in a text editor.

ocr-pdf.name: OCR PDF
ocr-pdf.description: Make a scanned PDF searchable with OCR, or extract the recognized text.

ai-summarizer.name: Summarize PDF
ai-summarizer.description: Summarize a PDF with AI so you can read the main points without opening every page.

translate-pdf.name: Translate PDF
translate-pdf.description: Translate PDF content into another language and download the result.
